subject: DPIA & training-attestation request — Medisphere (LLM inputs / retention / SCCs)
messages:
From: Marcel DuPont <marcel.dpo@medisphere.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: DPIA / attestations needed for LLM training on customer inputs

Hi Sean,

We are preparing an internal DPIA for a prospective deployment of Redwood for several clinical-note summarization flows. Our privacy team needs clear, signed answers and evidence on a few items before we proceed to procurement:

1) Do you use customer prompt or response data to further train or fine-tune models (including for feature engineering, ranking, or safety datasets)? If yes, how is consent captured and how can a customer opt out?

2) What retention windows do you have for prompts and responses in hosted API vs Dedicated/Private? Can we configure a no-retain option?

3) Can you provide SOC 2 and CAIQ/SIG artifacts, and an attestation that for this account Medisphere data will not be used for model training?

4) We need to understand cross-border flows and whether you will sign SCCs and include controls for pseudonymization or tokenization of PII in logs.

Please send any standard attestation language you can sign, the relevant artifacts (SOC 2, DPA exhibit), and a short technical note describing how we would opt out of any training/aggregation pipelines.

Thanks — tight timeline for our DPIA review this week.

Marcel DuPont
DPO, Medisphere Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>

Hi Marcel — thanks for the clear list. We can move quickly on this. High level answers up front:

- Redwood does not train or fine-tune customer models using customer prompts or responses by default for hosted customers. We provide explicit "no-train" configuration per account and active exclusion from any central training pipelines.
- Retention: hosted API default: 30 days ephemeral cache (used only for short-term safety and KV caching). Dedicated/Private: by default data retention is 0 days in the control plane (customer-owned). All retention windows are configurable and we can commit to 0-day retention for your account.
- We can sign SCCs and execute the DPA. SOC 2 report and DPA exhibit attached.

I'm attaching our SOC 2 report and a draft DPA Annex A. I've also pulled a short architecture note that the infra team can expand on (internal no-train controls and how KV cache works).

I cc'd Rachel Kim (legal) and Aditya Rao (infra). Rachel — can you confirm standard attestation language we can sign for an enterprise no-train commitment and confirm SCCs? Aditya — can you add a 1-paragraph technical description of how customer inputs are excluded from any model training pipelines and retention controls?

Next steps: if you prefer, we can provide a signed attestation PDF and a short conferencing slot for your privacy team tomorrow.

Best,

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 16:30:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPIA / attestations needed for LLM training on customer inputs

Sean / Rachel — quick tech note below (for external consumption I suggest a lightly redacted version). Key points to include in the attestation: 

- In hosted mode we maintain an isolated request path per tenant. By default requests may be used for short-lived safety telemetry and batching heuristics inside the serving runtime, but we have an account-level "no-train" flag that:
  * prevents any copy of prompts/responses being forwarded to any central training/feature pipelines,
  * disables ingestion into data lakes used for model improvements,
  * turns off long-term safety corpus exports for that tenant.
- Ephemeral KV cache: used to accelerate generation (prefix caching). Default TTL is 30 days for hosted but TTL is configurable. For Dedicated and Private, TTL defaults to 0 and all caches can be configured to be ephemeral-only in RAM with no disk persistence.
- Logs: request-level metadata (latency, error codes) kept separately from content. Content redaction hooks exist (regex-based PII filters) and we support customer-supplied redaction callbacks for private deployments.

Suggested attestation wording to hand to Legal: "Redwood Inference will not use Medisphere prompts, responses, or derived artifacts for model training, tuning, or algorithmic improvement unless Medisphere provides explicit written consent. Redwood will enforce the customer 'no-train' configuration at the account and deployment level and will provide proof of exclusion on request."

I've attached the short architecture note and a minimal config snippet customers can apply. If you want, I can export an operational proof (log lines showing exclusion events) for the initial audit.

— Aditya
Lead Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Marcel DuPont <marcel.dpo@medisphere.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 09:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: DPIA / attestations needed for LLM training on customer inputs

Hi Marcel — wrapping up from Legal. We can sign an attestation and execute the DPA + SCCs for EU processing. A few clarifications and an explicit commitment we typically include: 

1) Attestation: we will provide a signed PDF attesting to the no-train commitment for Medisphere, with the following binding language (we are prepared to execute on company letterhead):
"Redwood Inference attests that for the Medisphere account and associated deployments, Redwood will not use customer prompts, completions, or derivative artifacts for model training, tuning, or feature engineering, unless Medisphere provides prior written consent. Redwood will apply account-level technical controls to ensure exclusion from training pipelines and will provide audit logs of the exclusion on request."

2) Retention and configuration: we can set hosted account retention to 0 days upon contract signature; alternatively we can set a short TTL (e.g., 24–72 hours) depending on your DPIA preference. For Dedicated/Private, default control plane retention is 0. We will include an annex in the DPA that codifies the retention window and control options.

3) SCCs & pseudonymization: we will sign EU SCCs. For pseudonymization we recommend the following options which we can include as contractual controls or runbooks:
  - customer-side tokenization of direct identifiers before sending (supported by our SDKs),
  - redaction hooks in the request pipeline (configurable),
  - hashed request-id mapping stored only in HSM-backed metadata stores for debugging requests for a limited window.

4) Evidence we can provide immediately: SOC 2 report (attached), CAIQ/SIG summary on request, and a short operational proof (sanitized logs) showing the no-train flag in effect for an account. We can provide a DocuSign-ready attestation PDF and a technical appendix.

Please confirm which retention profile you prefer and whether you want the attestation executed now or after PO/contract signature. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with your privacy team tomorrow.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
